title: The Immortal Game
line: Anderssen against Kieseritzky, London 1851: a bishop, both rooks and the queen given for mate.

steps.text: London, 1851. Anderssen has given a bishop, but his pieces are out. Most of Black's pieces are still at home.
Jump the knight to the center. It attacks the queen.
steps.after: Black's queen takes a pawn and attacks your rook in the corner.

steps.text: Anderssen left both rooks hanging and cut off Black's king with his bishop. Engines rate it level: Black could take a rook with check.
Black took the other rook instead, and that lost. Push the pawn on e4: it cuts Black's queen off from the squares near its king.
steps.after: Engines find a quicker way with the queen, but this one works too. Black takes the last rook, with check.

steps.text: Step out of the check with your king.
steps.after: Black brings out a knight, too late.

steps.text: Take on g7 with the knight, with check.
Give the queen with check. Taking her or blocking with the knight both lose at once.
steps.after: The knight left g8, so it no longer guards e7.
Checkmate, with two knights and a bishop. Anderssen gave a bishop, both rooks and his queen.

summary: Anderssen gave up piece after piece to keep the initiative. With Black's pieces at home, the rest mated.
